Leading the pack is **Hamilton**, which continues to prove why it remains the gold standard for contemporary musical theater. Close behind, **Maybe Happy Ending** has emerged as one of the season's most pleasant surprises—a robot love story that critics praise for its originality and unexpected emotional depth. Whether you're drawn to revolutionary storytelling, spectacular stagecraft, or sharp-witted comedy, March 2026 offers compelling options across the theatrical spectrum. Use the detailed reviews and ratings below to find the show that best matches your interests.

Leading the pack is **Oh, Mary!**, Cole Escola's absurdist reimagining of Mary Todd Lincoln as a cabaret-obsessed, hard-drinking narcissist. The production proves that sharp writing and committed performances can triumph without relying on technological spectacle.

**Harry Potter and the Cursed Child** continues to enchant audiences with its renowned stagecraft, earning an 82 from 69 reviews. Critics consistently highlight the production's magical illusions and technical achievements, though opinions remain divided on the narrative itself. Despite impressive special effects that critics universally applaud, the three-hour prequel struggles with narrative cohesion, reflected in its 66 score from 35 reviews. The production exemplifies a growing trend of screen-to-stage adaptations that prioritize spectacle over storytelling.

Whether you're drawn to intimate comedy, magical stagecraft, or effects-driven spectacle, March 2026 offers distinct theatrical experiences across the spectrum. Consider what matters most in your theatergoing experience before booking your tickets.

The five productions that managed to premiere before the industry's historic shutdown reveal both the diversity of that season's programming and the enduring quality that has allowed these shows to remain in cultural memory.

Leading our rankings is **Les Misérables**, which earns an 83/100 critic score for its grittier reboot at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre. This reimagined production demonstrates how classic musicals can find new relevance through bold artistic choices, though the approach doesn't win universal approval from traditionalists.

**A Soldier's Play** follows closely with a 78/100, marking the long-overdue Broadway debut of Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama. Critics consistently highlight the production's stellar ensemble work and the play's continued resonance in examining racial dynamics within American institutions.

The remaining entries showcase Broadway's range: Laura Linney's solo turn in **My Name is Lucy Barton** divides critics between admiration for her performance and questions about the adaptation's theatrical viability, while **Grand Horizons** offers boulevard comedy elevated by veteran performers Jane Alexander and James Cromwell. Rounding out the list, Ivo van Hove's radical **West Side Story** reimagining proves predictably polarizing, with critics split between those embracing its visceral innovations and those finding the experimental approach misguided.

With an average critic score of 74/100 across these five productions, the class of 2020 represents solid if not exceptional theatrical work. For those exploring this era's offerings, these rankings provide a starting point for understanding which productions have best stood the test of time.

Meanwhile, **The Little Mermaid the Musical** and **Gobstopper** round out the early offerings, both awaiting their critical debuts.

With an average critical score of 40 out of 100 across reviewed productions, the 2026 musical season reflects Broadway's ongoing challenge of balancing innovation with audience expectations. The wide variance in reception—from enthusiastic praise to lukewarm responses—underscores how even well-known properties require fresh creative vision to resonate with contemporary audiences.

As more productions open and accumulate reviews throughout the spring, theatergoers should monitor how these shows develop and which productions gain momentum with both critics and audiences.

best-broadway-plays-2020.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays from 2020

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway plays that opened in 2020 represent a fascinating snapshot of theater just before—and in some cases, just after—the pandemic shutdown that would reshape the industry. These five productions, averaging a solid 74/100 in critical reception, showcase the range of ambition and artistry that defined this pivotal moment.

Leading the pack is a grittier reimagining of **Les Misérables** at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre, earning an 83/100 across 9 reviews. Critics largely embrace this fresh take on the classic, though the production's darker approach doesn't win universal approval. Close behind, **A Soldier's Play** (78/100, 29 reviews) finally brings Charles Fuller's Pulitzer-winning drama to Broadway in a stellar revival that critics agree proves the work's enduring relevance and power.

The remaining productions demonstrate Broadway's willingness to experiment with varying degrees of success. **My Name is Lucy Barton** divides critics at 71/100, with Laura Linney's acclaimed solo performance anchoring Elizabeth Strout's intimate novel adaptation. **Grand Horizons**, also at 71/100, offers more traditional boulevard comedy about late-life divorce, elevated by veteran performers Jane Alexander and James Cromwell. Meanwhile, **West Side Story** (68/100) proves the most polarizing entry, with director Ivo van Hove's radical reinterpretation—complete with video design and unconventional staging—inspiring both passionate praise and skeptical resistance.

Whether you're drawn to bold reimaginings of classics or powerful dramatic revivals, these 2020 productions offer diverse perspectives on what Broadway play production can achieve.

best-broadway-plays-2021.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2021

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway productions that debuted in 2021 represent a remarkable period of theatrical innovation and renewal. That season marked Broadway's emotional return following an unprecedented shutdown, and the shows that emerged reflect both artistic ambition and cultural urgency.

The standout productions from this cohort demonstrate exceptional range. **Dana H.** leads the pack with its unconventional docudrama format, earning widespread acclaim for Deirdre O'Connell's mesmerizing lip-sync performance that brings a harrowing true story to life. **The Lehman Trilogy** stands as an epic theatrical achievement, with critics praising its extraordinary performances and stunning direction in chronicling the rise and fall of an American financial dynasty. Meanwhile, **Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club** earns recognition for Rebecca Frecknall's immersive reimagining that completely transforms the Playhouse Theatre into a decadent nightclub experience.

The 2021 season also showcased powerful solo performances in **Lackawanna Blues**, verbatim documentary theatre in **Is This a Room**, and vital reimaginings of classic works like **Company**. The diversity of voices is particularly notable, with **Pass Over** serving as Broadway's official reopening production and **Clyde's** offering Lynn Nottage's compassionate examination of redemption and second chances.

With an average critic score of 81/100 across these ten productions, the class of 2021 demonstrates consistently strong artistic merit. Whether you're drawn to experimental documentary theatre, sweeping historical dramas, or bold reinterpretations of musical theatre classics, these shows that have endured into 2026 offer compelling reasons to experience live theatre at its most innovative.

best-broadway-plays-2022.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2022

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway season of 2022 stands out as a remarkable year that brought audiences an extraordinary collection of new productions and revivals. This curated selection of 10 shows, averaging an impressive 83/100 critic score, represents the season's most acclaimed theatrical achievements.

Leading the pack is **Kimberly Akimbo**, the quirky musical about a teenager with a rare aging condition that critics have embraced as a near-perfect gem, balancing hilarious comedy with profound emotional depth. Close behind, two productions share equally strong acclaim: Nico Muhly and Stephen Sondheim's **Into the Woods** revival strips away spectacle to reveal the musical's dark heart in what critics call a triumphant tribute to the late composer, while Michael R. Jackson's **A Strange Loop** brings its Pulitzer Prize-winning meta-theatrical brilliance to Broadway with brazenly original storytelling that pushes boundaries.

The season proved particularly rich in Pulitzer Prize winners making their Broadway debuts or returning in new productions. Suzan-Lori Parks' **Topdog/Underdog** crackles with renewed energy, while Paula Vogel's **How I Learned to Drive**, Stephen Adly Guirgis's **Between Riverside and Crazy**, and Martyna Majok's **Cost of Living** each demonstrate why these plays earned American theater's highest honor. Tom Stoppard's **Leopoldstadt** adds the gravitas of a master playwright's deeply personal Holocaust meditation, while Jordan E. Cooper's **Ain't No Mo'** delivers audacious satirical comedy.

Whether you're planning your next theater outing or simply exploring what made 2022 such a standout year for Broadway, these critically acclaimed productions offer a diverse range of theatrical experiences worth discovering.

best-broadway-plays-2023.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays of 2023

As Broadway continues to thrive in March 2026, the plays that opened in 2023 remain a testament to one of the most artistically vibrant seasons in recent memory. This collection of ten productions showcases the remarkable range of American theatre, from long-awaited revivals to groundbreaking new works.

The standout among revivals is **Merrily We Roll Along**, Maria Friedman's transformative production that finally unlocked the emotional power of Sondheim's once-maligned musical. Critics have embraced it as a triumphant redemption, proving that great material sometimes simply needs the right moment and approach. Meanwhile, **Appropriate** has established itself as essential contemporary drama, with Branden Jacobs-Jenkins's searing family portrait—anchored by Sarah Paulson's commanding performance—earning recognition as a modern masterpiece.

The season also demonstrated Broadway's expanding creative boundaries. **Stranger Things: The First Shadow** defied skepticism about IP adaptations with technically stunning stagecraft that transcends its source material, while **Stereophonic** captivated audiences with its immersive three-hour journey into a 1970s recording studio. The class of 2023 further includes timely revivals like **Parade** and **Purlie Victorious**, Pulitzer Prize winner **Fat Ham**, and intimate solo work **Just for Us**.

With an average critical score of 82/100 across these ten productions, the 2023 season represents a high-water mark for theatrical excellence. Whether you're drawn to classic musicals reimagined, urgent contemporary voices, or ambitious theatrical spectacle, these productions offer compelling reasons to experience live theatre at its finest.

best-broadway-plays-2024.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays Opening in March 2026

As Broadway enters March 2026, the shows that debuted in 2024 continue to demonstrate remarkable staying power and critical acclaim. This collection of ten productions—averaging an impressive 83/100 critical score—represents some of the most inventive and emotionally resonant theater to reach New York stages in recent years.

Leading the pack is **Stereophonic**, David Adjmi's meticulously crafted drama about a 1970s rock band in the studio. With a score of 88/100 across 22 reviews, critics consistently describe it as a theatrical marvel that captures the messy, exhilarating reality of the creative process. Close behind is **Operation Mincemeat**, the grassroots British sensation that earned its Broadway transfer through sheer word-of-mouth momentum, with reviewers praising its inventive ensemble work and infectious energy.

The year also brought notable diversity in storytelling approaches. **Maybe Happy Ending** offers an unexpectedly poignant robot love story that critics call one of Broadway's most original musicals in years, while Cole Escola's **Oh, Mary!** reimagines Mary Todd Lincoln as a boozy, cabaret-obsessed narcissist in what reviewers hail as a comedic tour de force. More traditional revivals also shine, with Audra McDonald bringing fresh interpretation to Mama Rose in **Gypsy** and a lavish new production of **Oliver!** balancing spectacle with Dickensian grit.

From intimate character studies like **Mary Jane** to ambitious historical epics like **Suffs**, the 2024 Broadway season proves that audiences remain hungry for both innovation and substance. Whether you're drawn to experimental dance-musicals or classic revivals reimagined, these productions offer compelling reasons to experience live theater at its finest.

best-broadway-plays-2025.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays Opening in 2025

As March 2026 arrives, the Broadway plays that opened throughout 2025 continue to demonstrate the enduring power of theatrical storytelling. This season proves particularly strong, with ten productions earning an impressive average critic score of 85/100—a testament to the quality and ambition on display across Manhattan's stages.

Leading the field is Ivo van Hove's stripped-down revival of **All My Sons**, which earns widespread acclaim for transforming Arthur Miller's classic into a visceral, emotionally devastating experience. Van Hove's minimalist approach allows the ensemble cast to shine, resulting in what critics consider one of the most powerful productions of the season.

The year also brings successful revivals of beloved musicals, including a triumphant 20th-anniversary staging of **The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee** that critics describe as both joyous and tender, and a stirring new production of **Ragtime** that feels urgently relevant to contemporary audiences. Family audiences, meanwhile, have embraced **Paddington The Musical**, where a remarkably lifelike bear puppet has become a genuine theatrical marvel.

Among new works, Sanaz Toossi's Pulitzer Prize-winning **English** continues to earn strong notices for its nuanced exploration of language and identity, while Branden Jacobs-Jenkins delivers another characteristically sharp family drama with **Purpose**. The season's range extends from Arden Wohl's ambitious feminist memory play **Liberation** to the darkly comic **Dead Outlaw**, a musical chronicling outlaw Elmer McCurdy's bizarre posthumous journey.

Whether you're drawn to classic American drama, inventive new plays, or revivals that speak to our current moment, this season offers exceptional theatrical experiences across the spectrum.

best-broadway-plays-2026.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays of 2026

March 2026 brings a notably lean opening schedule for new Broadway plays, with just one production making its debut this month. While the limited roster reflects the challenging economics facing straight plays on Broadway, the sole entry demonstrates the enduring appeal of well-crafted psychological drama.

**Bug** stands as the month's singular offering, marking the long-awaited Broadway premiere of Tracy Letts' 1996 psychological thriller. With a solid critic score of 74/100 across 35 reviews, the production earns mostly positive notices for its intense exploration of paranoia and delusion. Originally produced by Chicago's Red Orchid Theatre three decades ago, the play arrives on Broadway with renewed relevance, its themes of conspiracy and fractured reality resonating in contemporary discourse. Critics particularly praise the production's claustrophobic staging and committed performances, though some note the material's deliberately unsettling nature may not appeal to all theatergoers.

The sparse March schedule underscores a broader trend in commercial theater, where plays increasingly struggle to secure Broadway berths amid rising production costs and risk-averse producers. That **Bug** makes it to the Great White Way at all speaks to both the strength of Letts' reputation—bolstered by his Pulitzer Prize-winning **August: Osage County**—and the theater community's ongoing commitment to provocative, challenging work.

For audiences seeking substantive dramatic fare this month, **Bug** offers a compelling if confronting option that showcases the raw power of theatrical storytelling. Those planning their spring theater calendar should consider catching this production while monitoring announcements for upcoming play openings in the months ahead.
